{{Short description|Mathematics research and teaching centre in Cambridge, England}}

[[File:CMS Central Core 01.jpg|thumb|Centre for Mathematical Sciences, Cambridge]]
The '''Faculty of Mathematics''' at the [[University of Cambridge]] comprises the '''Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics''' ('''DPMMS''') and the '''Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics''' ('''DAMTP'''). It is housed in the [[Centre for Mathematical Sciences (Cambridge)|Centre for Mathematical Sciences]] site in West [[Cambridge]], alongside the [[Isaac Newton Institute]]. Many distinguished mathematicians have been members of the faculty.

==Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics==
The Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics (DPMMS) was created in 1964 under the headship of [[W. V. D. Hodge|Sir William Hodge]].<ref name=whittle>{{Citation | first1=P. | last1=Whittle | author-link=Peter Whittle (mathematician) | title=The Cambridge Statistical Laboratory up to 1993 (revised 2002) | url=http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/History/2history.html | access-date=30 April 2009 | archive-date=19 December 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219080017/http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/History/2history.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>  It was housed in a converted warehouse at 16 Mill Lane, adjacent to its sister department DAMTP, until its move around 2000 to the present [[Centre for Mathematical Sciences (Cambridge)|Centre for Mathematical Sciences]] where it occupies Pavilions C, D, and E.

===Heads of department===
*1964–1969 [[W. V. D. Hodge]]
*1969–1984 [[J. W. S. Cassels]]
*1984–1991 [[D. J. H. Garling]]
*1991–1997 [[John H. Coates]]
*1997–2002 [[W. B. R. Lickorish]]
*2002–2007 [[Geoffrey Grimmett]]
*2007–2014 [[Martin Hyland]]
*2014–2018 [[Gabriel Paternain]]
*2018–2023 [[James R. Norris|James Norris]]
*since 2023 [[Ivan Smith (mathematician)|Ivan Smith]]

===Statistical Laboratory===
The Statistical Laboratory is a Sub-Department of DPMMS.<ref>{{Citation |title=Statutes and Ordinances of the University of Cambridge |url=http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/univ/so/pdfs/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090428064010/http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/univ/so/pdfs/ |archive-date=2009-04-28 }}</ref> It was created in 1947 with accommodation in a "temporary hut", and was established on 21 March 1953 within the Faculty of Mathematics.<ref name=whittle/> It moved in 1958 to the basement of the new Chemistry Department in Lensfield Road, and then formed part of the new Department (DPMMS) in Mill Lane on its creation in 1964. It occupies Pavilion D of the [[Centre for Mathematical Sciences (Cambridge)|Centre for Mathematical Sciences]].

==Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics==
[[Image:Centre for mathematical sciences cambridge.jpg|thumb|Department of Applied Mathematics & Theoretical Physics is based at [[Centre for Mathematical Sciences (Cambridge)|Centre for Mathematical Sciences]].]]

The Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics (DAMTP) was founded by [[George Batchelor]] in 1959, and for many years was situated on Silver Street, in the former office buildings of [[Cambridge University Press]].<ref name=crighton>{{cite web|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/about/history.html|title=History of DAMTP|publisher=DAMTP}}</ref> However since the opening of the [[Isaac Newton Institute]] in 1991, the Department has been located at the [[Centre for Mathematical Sciences (Cambridge)]]. Theoretical Physics (including [[cosmology]], [[theory of relativity|relativity]], and [[high energy physics]]) occupies most of Pavilion B, while Applied Mathematics (including [[fluid dynamics]] and [[solid mechanics]]) occupies most of Pavilions F, G, and H.

===Heads of department===
*1959–1983 [[George Batchelor]]
*1983–1991 [[Keith Moffatt]]
*1991–2000 [[David Crighton]]
*2000–2005 [[Timothy J. Pedley]]
*2005–2015 [[Peter H. Haynes|Peter Haynes]]
*2015–2020 Nigel Peake
*2020–present Colm-Cille Patrick Caulfield
